From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Recommendation key:** Reject = do not accept, counter with playbook position. Counter = move toward playbook position. Assess = diligence needed before a position. Open = leave unresolved.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000). The 20% cap is a fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Recommendation: Reject, counter at 25%.** Do not concede 20% without written authority, and the Seller's "FINAL" label does not bind us.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, excess-only (only the amount above the basket is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller's structure leaves the first AUD 250,000 unrecoverable.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). Fundamental and fraud claims sit outside this limit.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The "applies to all Claims" wording would pull fundamental and fraud claims into the general period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Merging these into the general regime removes the protection title is meant to provide.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller's wording would let limitations apply to fraud claims.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter 1.1 discloses the entire data room as at 22 September 2026 (including DD-002 to DD-012). 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Schedule 7 relies on general disclosure.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** General disclosure would deem every data-room document disclosed against the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test that would swallow the warranties.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3,600,000). No final written consent, and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Make effective consent and condition satisfaction a condition precedent. Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion.
- **Disclosure:** Not repaid. No final discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation: Reject the post-completion release.** Require repayment and discharge at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure:** Bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. On-cost treatment is not stated.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific funds flow line item or seller funding, including triggered on-costs. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation: Reject the silent exclusion.** Require the amount and triggered on-costs to be itemised and seller-funded.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate."
- **Disclosure:** DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which is not bank verification. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not verified either way.
- **Recommendation: Counter, broaden.** Do not accept the "adequate" characterisation.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure:** A download link went to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. It is not established whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. No loss amount stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the "not material" conclusion.** Require log preservation, an investigation, and regular updates. Do not quantify it.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals, AUD 330,000 aggregate, described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure:** Does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together for timing and scope.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: Assess.** Request the contract terms, timing and termination rights. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet. No price deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept separate. No hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Routing these through the general regime overrides the separate protections.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Disclosure:** DD-012 is the source relied on. It does not confirm the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation: Reject as sufficient.** Require independent evidence, such as an ASIC company extract, a certified register, share transfer documents, PPSR and other encumbrance searches, and evidence of the Seller's authority to sell.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation: Keep Open, reject "settled."** These terms are not agreed.

---

## Decisions and Actions Needed

1. **Amelia Frost approvals.** Any concession on the 20% cap (AUD 4.8m), the 18-month period, or a post-completion Riverlark release needs her prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given, so these stay at playbook positions.
2. **Not agreed at principal level.** The Seller's claim that positions were "settled at principal level" and are "not intended to be re-opened" has no Buyer sign-off in the record. Do not treat them as agreed.
3. **Market claims.** The Seller's market ranges are unsourced. They do not change the playbook positions.
4. **Stale data room.** The disclosure is as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Request a refreshed data room and disclosure update before negotiating further.
